opportunities.summary: Revitalizing Rituals Research-creation with Local Communities (Tunisia, Hungary) Deadline: 19 Jul 2026
opportunities.details: Revitalizing Rituals Research-creation with Local Communities (Tunisia, Hungary) Read this call in: Hungarian Revitalizing Rituals invites artists from all disciplines — sound, movement, visual arts, installation, performance and transdisciplinary practices — to take part in a research-creation journey across two interstitial landscapes: Bhar Lazreg in Tunisia and the transforming wetlands of Somogy County in Hungary. The Revitalizing Rituals project is looking for artists interested in rituals as living forms of belonging: ways to reconnect communities, land, memory, food, ecological reciprocity and the more-than-human world. Selected artists will work with local communities not as subjects, but as co-participants in a shared artistic inquiry into how we can move from extraction toward reciprocity. In total, four artists will be selected: two artists in Hungary and two artists in Tunisia. In each location, one locally connected artist and one artist from a migration or diaspora background linked to the region will take part in the residency. Artists apply individually (or as collectives) and will each develop their own artistic process in dialogue with the local community. The journey begins with a shared Placemaking camp, for artists and partners to explore relational forms and knowledge. This is followed by a four-month residency process (April–July 2027) combining onsite work, research, and experimentation. Each residency process will manifest in artistic gestures. The …

This residency takes place in a nature-based, rural environment, where artists live and work together under camping conditions. The focus is not only on creating artworks, but on reimagining the campsite itself as an artistic, social, and cultural space. Central question is: How can a hiking campground become a cultural oasis? And how can an off-site residency be meaningfully connected to a downtown theatre? The Mátra residency creates a dialogue between the downtown theatre and an off-site, nature-based location, treating distance not as a barrier, but as an opportunity for connection, exchange, and new forms of presence. A total of 8 artists will be selected (5 international + 3 Hungary-based) across the following areas: visual arts / spatial practices performing arts storytelling / media design / architecture digital / hybrid practices This open call is open to individual artists and cultural practitioners working across disciplines within the cultural and creative sectors. Applicants must be resident in a Creative Europe participating country (EU Member States and associated countries), have an active artistic or creative practice, and be able to work in English and in an international, collaborative environment. Under pressure from the war, public consciousness has been raised on the importance of keeping hold of tangible and intangible Ukrainian heritage that might be lost, while Cyprus has been dealing with the heritage of loss in multiple ways over the last 50 years. opportunities.title: Spazio13: Urban Bodies Residency 2026 on Migration (Italy)
opportunities.summary: Spazio13: Urban Bodies Residency 2026 on Migration (Italy) Deadline: 30 Jul 2026
opportunities.details: Spazio13: Urban Bodies Residency 2026 on Migration (Italy) Urban Bodies is an international artistic residency hosted by Spazio13 in Bari, Italy, from 1 October to 27 November 2026. The programme will welcome four international artists and cultural practitioners to investigate the relationship between contemporary migration, urban transformation and the body as a site of memory, negotiation and belonging. The residency takes place in the Libertà neighbourhood, one of Bari’s most densely populated areas and one of the urban districts with the highest concentration of foreign residents in the city. Libertà is marked by significant socioeconomic fragilities, while at the same time, it is one of Bari’s most dynamic urban thresholds. Urban Bodies starts from the recognition that contemporary Mediterranean migration is entering a phase of increasing intensity and complexity. The programme will unfold through four phases: territorial research and community encounter; co-creation and design; artistic production; and public restitution. The residency will select four European artists, cultural practitioners, designers and researchers, specifically one profile for each of the following fields: performance, theatre, dance, movement, sound and embodied practices; visual arts, photography, video, installation, public art and image-based research; material design, spatial practices, ecological design, craft and experimental making; sociology, urban studies, cultural research, …

opportunities.summary: Fundación Camila Cañeque/BAR project: Residency Programme 2026 (Spain) Deadline: 31 Jul 2026
opportunities.details: Fundación Camila Cañeque/BAR project: Residency Programme 2026 (Spain) Read this call in: Spanish The Fundación Camila Cañeque Residency Programme supports artistic, curatorial, writing and research-based practices grounded in critical thinking, conceptual exploration and open-ended inquiry. In 2026, Fundación Camila Cañeque and BAR project present an international open call for one six-week residency (8 October to 20 November 2026) at Mas Verd, Fundación Camila Cañeque’s residence in the Empordà, Catalonia. The residency is particularly well suited to practices that benefit from time, focused attention, contextual exchange and professional dialogue, especially those that do not depend on conventional production infrastructure. The residency proposes pause as a working methodology, offering a framework for research, reflection and experimentation in which not everything needs to be resolved, produced or concluded. A patron funds one year’s work for each Fellow. For this first 2026 call for applications, projects will focus on two themes: ‘disinformation and narrative wars’ and ‘political and social changes in the Gulf’. opportunities.title: Indonesia | ASEAN Artists Residency for Myanmar artists
opportunities.summary: Indonesia | ASEAN Artists Residency for Myanmar artists Residencies deadline: 31 Jul 2026
opportunities.details: Indonesia | ASEAN Artists Residency for Myanmar artists The ASEAN Secretariat is inviting Myanmar artists to participate in the ASEAN Artists Residency Programme (AARP), between 1 – 31 October 2026 (TBC) in Jakarta, Indonesia. The programme is designed to explore ASEAN identities and deepen mutual understanding across diverse global cultures. Under this programme, the selected artist will produce one original artwork during the one-month residency period , which will be donated to the ASEAN Gallery’s permanent collection. The artist is expected to work in a studio format and participate in activities and events organised by ASEAN Member States and the ASEAN Secretariat. At a minimum, the artist must produce a painting in acrylic, batik, Chinese brush, collage, crayon, ink, mixed media, oil, watercolour, or any other media . Collages, two-dimensional embossed paintings, and three-dimensional paintings are also acceptable. Other mediums may be acceptable subject to selection committee approval. Support 1-month accommodation Return airfare and travel costs Artwork production costs Daily stipend during the residency duration Studio space Presentation of artwork at the ASEAN Gallery Social media visibility AARP application guidelines Deadline: 31 July 2026

opportunities.title: Poland | Research residency 2026 for Europe-based artists
opportunities.summary: Poland | Research residency 2026 for Europe-based artists Residencies deadline: 31 Jul 2026
opportunities.details: Poland | Research residency 2026 for Europe-based artists Konrad and Paweł Jarodzki Artist-in-Residence Programme at the Krzyżowa Foundation for Mutual Understanding in Europe is calling for artists to develop research-based projects in dialogue with the site's history, educational activities, and contemporary social challenges. The residency will take place in Krzyżowa, Poland, from 21 September to 31 October 2026. During artists’ stay in Krzyżowa, they have an opportunity to focus both on their individual and joint work and on interacting with groups participating in the exchanges of the International Youth Meeting Centre. The organisers dedicate the residency programme to artistic practices that are sensitive to the social and natural environment and that are committed to working through the past or experimenting with the future . They support a diversity of attitudes, media and artistic practices, and examine how, with the help of art, it is possible to engage in dialogue and make intercultural connections. They operate in an international artistic environment, rooted in Central and Eastern Europe, Lower Silesia and in the history of Polish-German dialogue. opportunities.details: Hypha_etc: Night as Commons Residency 2026 for Europe-based Artists (Romania) Hypha_etc is calling for applications from Europe-based artists for a residency in Vármező / Câmpu Cetății, Transylvania, Romania, from 1 October – 10 November 2026. Night as Commons explores darkness as a shared ecological, cultural and political condition. In a world increasingly shaped by artificial illumination, night has been fragmented, colonised and rendered scarce. Darkness — once a universal temporal commons — is now overshadowed by infrastructures that extend productivity, disrupt biological rhythms, and reshape the behaviour of humans and non‑humans alike. The residency invites artistic and research‑based practices that engage with — or depart from — themes such as: night‑time ecologies and photoperiodicity the cultural, poetic or symbolic dimensions of darkness sensory experience, perception and orientation temporal critique, labour and the politics of illumination speculative, spatial or ecological approaches to ‘unbuilding’ light light pollution, skyglow and disrupted rhythms The residency also offers interdisciplinary mentorship from experts in physics, biology and curatorial research, supporting both scientific grounding and artistic development. Applicants must be legally based in one of the Creative Europe countries including OCT/OR. Located on the island of Faial, near the Capelinhos Volcano (Azores, Portugal), the residency offers an immersion in a territory shaped by the power of geology, its insular nature, and the constant interplay between nature and human presence. More than just a workplace, the Azores here become living material for creation. AVISTAVULCÃO invites artists to develop projects that engage with the landscape, memory, local history, and the contemporary challenges facing peripheral regions. Themes such as geological time, transformation, resilience, isolation, mobility, and the relationships between communities and the environment may serve as starting points for processes of research and creation. AVISTAVULCÃO values context-sensitive proposals that prioritise observation, listening, and a relationship with the place. Throughout the residency, artists will have the opportunity to meet local stakeholders and engage in moments of sharing with the community, culminating in a public presentation of the process or the results of the work carried out. opportunities.title: Source Writing Prize 2026
opportunities.summary: Source Writing Prize 2026 Open Calls deadline: 01 Aug 2026
opportunities.details: Source Writing Prize 2026 Source Writing Prize is looking for new writers to contribute to Source. New writers can send an article; the winning entry will receive 500 GBP/570 EUR and they will either publish it or commission an article in the future. All short-listed entries will also be considered for publication or for future paid commissions. Most of the writing in Source takes a specific form: book reviews, exhibition reviews or texts introducing sets of pictures . But they are also interested in others forms of writing. Their interest in photography is not only about the photographs that appear in books and exhibitions; it touches most aspects of life and they like to read about those encounters too. This could be an article about a particular photograph of historical, aesthetic or biographical interest. It could be about some cultural or philosophical aspect of photography. It could be something they’ve not thought about. They enjoy writing that is thoughtful, funny, well researched and surprising. It could be personal or dispassionate. It could be fun, or deadly serious. It might shed new light on something they thought they knew or an introduction to something they’ve never heard of before. The rules: Writers should not have written for Source before. The article must be no more than 700 words . The article should not have been published previously. opportunities.title: Australia | BigCi Environmental Awards 2026
opportunities.summary: Australia | BigCi Environmental Awards 2026 Residencies deadline: 02 Aug 2026
opportunities.details: Australia | BigCi Environmental Awards 2026 BigCi, an independent, artist run, not for profit artist residency programme in Bilpin, Australia (near Sydney), is calling for applications for the 2026 BigCi Environmental Awards. Australian and international artists from various fields – visual art, installation, multimedia, performance, literature, music, photography, film making, curating – are invited to submit entries for the Awards. Two winners of the Awards will each receive 4 free weeks at the BigCi residency and 5,000 AUD prize money. The winning artists will have an opportunity to explore the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Wollemi, Blue Mountains and Gardens of Stone National Parks on guided walks and will be given research assistance relevant to their projects. At the end of their residencies, they will present their work at a BigCi Open Day event. BigCi 2026 application guidelines Deadline: 2 August 2026

opportunities.details: Justice and Peace Netherlands: Shelter City 2027 Fellowship for Human Rights Defenders (Netherlands) Credit: Maria Diaz Read this call in: French , Spanish Justice and Peace Netherlands is launching a new call for applications for human rights defenders at risk to participate in Shelter City Netherlands. Shelter City Netherlands is an initiative for short and temporary relocation for three months financed by Justice and Peace Netherlands, the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs, host organisations and municipalities. From March 2027 onwards, 14 cities in the Netherlands will receive human rights defenders for a period of three months. At the end of their stay in the Netherlands, participants are expected to return with new tools and energy to carry out their work at home. During their stay in the Netherlands, each human rights defender is independent and responsible for their own programme. In establishing this, human rights defenders will be supported by Justice and Peace and the hosting organisation in the city. Asser Institute Fellowship: In the context of the Institute’s Visiting Researchers Programme, the Asser Institute hosts one Fellow per year within the framework of the Shelter City initiative by Justice and Peace. The fellowship will take place in September 2027. The selected Fellow will carry out a research project during the three-month period and take part in other relevant human rights (research) activities of the Asser Institute. The call is for 4 Labs of 9 days, across 4 countries, hosted by ‘duos’ of academic and dance institutions: UNATC/CNDB (Romania), Tallinn University/STL (Estonia), Hochschule Düsseldorf/tanzhaus nrw (Germany), and Interactive Technologies Institute/O Espaço do Tempo (Portugal). The Labs will take place between December 2026 and February 2027. Part 1 of the Lab, on days 1-4, will take place in the academic partner leading the Lab, where there will be half-day master classes around the topic of the lab. Part 2 of the Lab, on days 6-9, will take place in the partner dance centre of the same country, with studio spaces. It will end with a series of internal presentations from each artist duo. Both applicants must be resident in a Creative Europe eligible country. opportunities.summary: 17th Gwangju Biennale Artistic Director job Open Calls deadline: 03 Aug 2026
opportunities.details: 17th Gwangju Biennale Artistic Director job The Gwangju Biennale Foundation has announced an international open call for the Artistic Director of the 17th Gwangju Biennale. The call is open to exhibition professionals and curators from around the world, regardless of nationality, gender, or age . Applications may be submitted by individuals or by teams of two or more co-artistic directors. Collaborative proposals involving both domestic and international professionals are also encouraged. The Foundation seeks innovative exhibition proposals that can artistically embody the spirit of Gwangju grounded in democracy, peace, and human rights while introducing new critical discourses and contributing to the advancement of contemporary art. Through this fully open process, the Foundation hopes to attract outstanding curators and exhibition-makers from Korea and abroad. Selection criteria A visionary and action-oriented leader capable of accumulating and expanding the region's cultural assets based on the pride and identity of Gwangju, while fostering future generations of local artistic directors. An expert who can redefine the Biennale's role in advancing contemporary art and take the lead in identifying and addressing key issues in today's art world. A strategist who can strengthen the unique brand value and international standing of the Gwangju Biennale, deeply rooted in the identity of the city and the institution. opportunities.details: Prague UNESCO City of Literature Residency for Writers and Translators 2027 (Czech Republic) Prague City of Literature offers an opportunity to writers and translators to live and work in the city centre where historical architecture meets modern and vibrant city life. This call is for eight two-month residencies in 2027 which will be held in: January – February March – April May – June July – August September – October November – December Applicants must have: Basic knowledge of English language At least one published literary work (not self-published) or two broadcast or published radio dramas or one carried out or published theatre play or at least one translated work of a Czech author Willingness to participate on the local literary life (author readings, meeting students, talks, activities arranged by the receiving institution or connected to the cultural events of the city) Working on the writings during the stay The accommodation and travel expenses are covered by Prague City of Literature; the residents will also receive a scholarship of 15,000 CZK (approx. 600 EUR per month). opportunities.title: Akademie Schloss Solitude: Web Residencies ‘Ignore All Previous Instructions’ 2026 (Online)
opportunities.summary: Akademie Schloss Solitude: Web Residencies ‘Ignore All Previous Instructions’ 2026 (Online) Deadline: 7 Aug 2026
opportunities.details: Akademie Schloss Solitude: Web Residencies ‘Ignore All Previous Instructions’ 2026 (Online) With the Web Residencies Call No. 22, !Mediengruppe Bitnik invites artists to create works that challenge extractive digital platforms and AI systems. For the tenth anniversary of the Web Residencies programme, Akademie Schloss Solitude look back at the first call in 2016, following up on its question on where to meet online when digital platforms are monopolised and weaponized – a problem we face now more than ever. This edition will explore how to interrupt dominant technological logics – from ad-tech surveillance to prompt injection vulnerabilities – to imagine alternative structures and communication methods. The programme seeks proposals that hijack, glitch, and disrupt rather than comply with existing systems, drawing on strategies like Situationist ‘détournement’ to map routes through and around the grids we are trapped within. Duration of Web Residencies is from 22 September to 22 October 2026, with an optional one-day online coding workshop on 17 September and the launch of the Web Residency projects in October/November 2026. Artists of all disciplines may apply. There is no age limit. The submission is free of charge. Six project proposals will be selected and rewarded with an online residency and a grant of 1,200 EUR. Deadline: 7 August 2026 More info & apply Technology & New Media Share this call: Share this call: See also: More opportunities with online and hybrid mobility

opportunities.title: Goethe-Institut: Confluence of Myths Residency for Lower Mekong Artists (Vietnam)
opportunities.summary: Goethe-Institut: Confluence of Myths Residency for Lower Mekong Artists (Vietnam) Deadline: 9 Aug 2026
opportunities.details: Goethe-Institut: Confluence of Myths Residency for Lower Mekong Artists (Vietnam) This artist residency programme invites art practitioners to join a one-month period of surveying, researching, and creating works around a shared interest in the concepts and processes of myth making in Trà Vinh, Vietnam. The residency is from 15 October to 15 November 2026 and in late December 2026 there will be a showcase at No Cai Bum Festival 2026. The residency will select four art practitioners from the Lower Mekong Subregion: Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Thailand, and Myanmar. The open call welcomes emerging practitioners (regardless of age) whose practice and interest engage with the intersections of culture, history, and linguistics, and/or explores the nature of linguistic fragmentation, ruptures, and absences. Writers with a focus on creative writing, allegorical narratives and critical fabulation are welcome, as are applicants interested in the process of making research-driven, experimental, or community-rooted methodologies. Selected artists will receive: An artist and production fee of up to 800 EUR Fully funded round-trip travel from the artist’s country of residence to Trà Vinh, Vietnam Accommodation, shared working space (including a simple ceramic studio), local transportation in Trà Vinh, and a living stipend of EUR 200 per person Curatorial and logistical support from a Vietnamese curator and local coordinator A weekly programme featuring local experts, including talks, …

opportunities.title: Labó Bosa: ‘The Economics of Being Looked At’ 2027 Residency (Italy)
opportunities.summary: Labó Bosa: ‘The Economics of Being Looked At’ 2027 Residency (Italy) Deadline: 10 Aug 2026
opportunities.details: Labó Bosa: ‘The Economics of Being Looked At’ 2027 Residency (Italy) Labó Bosa invites artists and cultural professionals to apply for The Economics of Being Looked At, a one-month residency exploring authenticity in a rural village and in art. The residency runs from 1 to 31 March 2027 and closes with an open studio. Bosa (Italy), like many villages, is under pressure to look the way visitors expect it to; artists face the same pull, towards what is legible, recognisable and sellable. Five artists from different disciplines will live and work together at Labó Bosa’s printmaking studio, a former tannery on the river Temo, reflecting on that question through their own practice and building a collaborative print edition together. The residency is open to artists and cultural professionals aged 18 or over, working individually, legally resident in a Creative Europe country other than Italy, and active in the visual arts or a related field. The residency is looking for artists and cultural practitioners, working individually across a range of disciplines (photography, painting, illustration, architecture, design and beyond), with an interest in printmaking, in questions of authenticity and place, and in collaborative, shared ways of making and living. No prior printmaking experience is required. opportunities.title: Lothringer 13 Halle: Curating Journalism Residency 2027 (Germany)
opportunities.summary: Lothringer 13 Halle: Curating Journalism Residency 2027 (Germany) Deadline: 10 Aug 2026
opportunities.details: Lothringer 13 Halle: Curating Journalism Residency 2027 (Germany) Lothringer 13 Halle, in cooperation with Artist-in-Residence Munich (the residency programme of the City of Munich), invites applications for three transdisciplinary residencies for professional cultural practitioners working at the intersection of art, journalism, and curating. The project Curating Journalism understands freedom of the press and artistic freedom as complementary conditions of a democratic public sphere. Their solidarity is a central cultural task of democratic societies. The residency is part of the research and exhibition project Curating Journalism and supports independent research-based projects exploring new connections between artistic, journalistic, and curatorial practice. The residency is from 8 January to 26 March 2027 in Ebenböckhaus, Munich, Germany. Applicants must have their primary place of residence within Europe and outside Bavaria. The residency includes: Monthly stipend (1,400 EUR/month) Production funding of up to 1,400 EUR per resident (up to 600 EUR for a public event at Ebenböckhaus and up to 800 EUR for the presentation of the project at Lothringer 13 Halle) Free accommodation Travel reimbursement within Europe (up to 350 EUR) Workspace at Lothringer 13 Halle Deadline: 10 August 2026 More info & apply Share this call: Share this call:

opportunities.title: British Council: Connections Through Culture Grants 2026
opportunities.summary: British Council: Connections Through Culture Grants 2026 Deadline: 12 Aug 2026
opportunities.details: British Council: Connections Through Culture Grants 2026 The British Council is calling for applications from artists or organisations for their Connections Through Culture (CTC) grants programme, which supports creative collaborations between the UK and select countries. Grants are available to support creative practitioners, cultural professionals, artists, organisations, festivals, biennials, hubs and collectives to develop and deliver projects across a range of themes and art forms. In 2026, CTC incorporates grants programmes formerly known as Biennials Connect (Visual Arts) and Architecture, Design and Fashion Biennials and Festivals Grants. It is also the major Arts grants programme for 2026, in place of International Collaboration Grants. Organisations and individuals are eligible to apply. Participating countries are: Albania, Argentina, Australia, Bangladesh, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Colombia, Mainland China, Egypt, Indonesia, Kazakhstan, Kenya, Kosovo, Lebanon, Malaysia, Mexico, Montenegro, New Zealand, Nigeria, North Macedonia, Pakistan, Palestine, Peru, Philippines, Saudi Arabia, Serbia, South Africa, Tanzania, Thailand, Tunisia, Turkey, United Arab Emirates, UK, Ukraine, Uzbekistan, Venezuela, and Vietnam. Each country partnership is eligible for a specific amount, ranging from 5,000 GBP to 15,000 GBP. opportunities.title: K3 | Tanzplan Hamburg: Residency Programme for Choreographers 2027–28 (Germany)
opportunities.summary: K3 | Tanzplan Hamburg: Residency Programme for Choreographers 2027–28 (Germany) Deadline: 12 Aug 2026
opportunities.details: K3 | Tanzplan Hamburg: Residency Programme for Choreographers 2027–28 (Germany) K3 | Tanzplan Hamburg provides three paid eight-month residencies to choreographers who are at the beginning of their career and have produced multiple choreographic works of their own. The residency begins in August 2027 and runs until April 2028. The goal of the residency is to develop and strengthen the connections between choreographic practice, research, artistic production, and qualification. The duration of eight months should provide sufficient time and space for overcoming conventional rhythms of production and open up opportunities for exchange with other artists. Applications in all choreographic fields are accepted (e.g. dance for young audience, public space, film) and from all countries. Applicants do not require a formal dance education. Applicants with disabilities and from marginalised communities are encouraged to apply. Only applications by individuals can be accepted. The residency programme covers: a monthly scholarship for living expenses and accommodation in Hamburg (exact amount to be confirmed, in the season 25/26 this was 2,500 EUR per month) one-time travel expenses from and to place of residence support in obtaining necessary papers/visa and related costs a moderate production budget for the performances at the end of the residency which allows for a small team over the last few weeks of the residency use of the K3 studios an accompanying support from the K3 team in …

TaDA – Textile and Design Alliance is a cultural promotion programme of the cantons of St. Gallen, Appenzell Ausserrhoden, and Thurgau. It enables experimental and innovative engagement with the textile and design culture of Eastern Switzerland and is conducted in collaboration with textile companies rooted in the region. TaDA annually offers six national and international personalities a work residency in Switzerland. The residents develop projects in the fields of art, design, architecture, literature, performing arts, or in interdisciplinary contexts. As programme partners, textile companies and institutions from Eastern Switzerland provide know-how and technology. This gives the residents the opportunity to carry out practical artistic work and applied research. The partners, in turn, count on creative exchange with the invitees. The residency will take place in Terni, Umbria (Italy), from 16 to 30 November 2026, and up to three artists or collectives will be selected. The call is open to artists and collectives of any age and geographical background, experienced and interested in performative, installation-based, participatory projects and hybrid formats in urban space. opportunities.title: Cité internationale des arts: Art, Society and Clinical Psychology Residency 2027 (France)
opportunities.summary: Cité internationale des arts: Art, Society and Clinical Psychology Residency 2027 (France) Deadline: 16 Aug 2026
opportunities.details: Cité internationale des arts: Art, Society and Clinical Psychology Residency 2027 (France) Read this call in: French Launched in 2025 by the Françoise Association and the Cité internationale des arts, this research and creative residency programme explores the links between contemporary art, psychiatry and the humanities. The residency will take place from 5 January to 26 March 2027. Conceived as an open research space, this programme is not a therapeutic programme. It is open to artists of all nationalities whose practice resonates with the notion of the ‘clinical’. This refers to a situated approach, as close as possible to the subject, ‘at the patient’s bedside’. Within the context of the residency, this approach shifts towards the artistic field: creation is envisaged here as a grounded, relational practice, attentive to the contexts in which it takes shape. The programme thus promotes approaches that remain as close as possible to real-life narratives and experiences, and which engage in a reflection on the challenges of care. The laureate will receive bespoke support from Albertine de Galbert, a clinical psychologist and exhibition curator, and from the programme’s partners. The residency programme has no age limit and is open to artists and creators from any discipline, at mid-career or established stage, and of any nationality. As part of the programme, the selected laureate will each receive: Dedicated professional support, meetings, and networking opportunities …

opportunities.title: Hong Kong | Art-Tech Convention 2026
opportunities.summary: Hong Kong | Art-Tech Convention 2026 Open Calls deadline: 17 Aug 2026
opportunities.details: Hong Kong | Art-Tech Convention 2026 The Indra and Harry Banga Gallery at City University of Hong Kong is calling for Network Presenters from across Asia for 10AFEST (8–10 October 2026), a convention dedicated to Art-Tech and Cultural Innovations, held in celebration of the Gallery’s 10th anniversary. The programme invites artists, researchers, and curators whose practice engages with the emerging trajectories of art, technology, and cultural innovation , cultivating Asian interdisciplinary discourse and fostering productive dialogue among artists, scholars, curators, innovators, and changemakers. Network Presenter will join twenty to twenty-five artists, researchers, and curators in offering a cross-sectional view of the region's current cultural landscape. Presentations are organised into six thematic tracks , with a dedicated panel matching each presentation to the track that best suits it. Eligibility The call is open to artists, scholars, curators, innovators, and changemakers based in Asia , or whose practice is rooted in the region, working at the intersection of art, technology, and cultural innovation . Presenters may share completed work, present case studies, or pitch an ongoing project at the convention. Support On-site accommodation and catering are provided for all Network Presenters. Application guidelines and more information about Indra and Harry Banga Gallery Deadline: 17 August 2026

opportunities.summary: Kunsthalle Görlitz: Group Exhibition on Granite and Gravity 2027 (Germany) Deadline: 20 Aug 2026
opportunities.details: Kunsthalle Görlitz: Group Exhibition on Granite and Gravity 2027 (Germany) Read this call in: German The group exhibition Granite and Gravity (18 September – 31 October 2027) explores connections between the deep bedrock beneath the Germany-Czech Republic-Poland border triangle and the universe. In the future, gravitational waves – tiny distortions of spacetime that can be detected using highly sensitive detectors and provide insights into the most distant events in the cosmos – are to be measured within the region’s massive granite massif. As part of the structural change following the phase-out of lignite mining, the German Center for Astrophysics (Deutsches Zentrum für Asrtophysic – DZA) is being established in Lusatia. New research infrastructures for astrophysics are being developed, including the Low Seismic Lab, which is to be built approximately 200 meters deep within the Lusatian granite massif. The open call is open to professional artists working in all disciplines of contemporary art who live or work primarily in Germany, Poland, or the Czech Republic. Individual artists and collectives are welcome. The project is seeking artistic projects in all media – including drawing, photography, sculpture, installation, video, sound, performance, painting, cross-media, and experimental formats. The exhibition welcomes existing works, concepts for new works to be created in time for the exhibition, as well as site-specific projects developed in Görlitz and/or in …

opportunities.details: FAKI Festival: Artists, Activists, Researchers and Theatre Critics 2027 (Croatia) FAKI Festival – International Festival of Alternative Theatrical Expression is calling for artists, activists, researchers and theatre critics to participate in its next edition happening in Zagreb, Croatia from 25 to 31 May 2027. The 30th edition of the FAKI Festival is celebrating more than a festival anniversary. Thirty years of FAKI also marks three decades of the organisation behind it: thirty years of self-organisation, collective work, artistic experimentation, friendships, disagreements, persistence and survival. This milestone invites us to pause, not out of nostalgia, but to ask what it means to celebrate today. The festival is interested in works that approach celebration not only as a subject, but also as a method: as a way of making, sharing and experiencing art together. The FAKI Festival will support with the following: Travel costs up to 200 EUR for individuals and up to 500 EUR for groups, with preference given to sustainable means of transport (bus, train, shared car) Shared accommodation on-site at AKC Medika and healthy vegan lunches and dinners during the festival Basic technical support (light, sound, and other wonders) Photo and video documentation of the performances Public relations and media presence via the festival network Rehearsal space/residency (if needed) Dramaturgy support and/or feedback (if needed) Deadline: 20 August 2026 More info & apply Share this call: …

opportunities.title: François Schneider Foundation: Contemporary Talents Competition ‘Earth’ First Edition (France)
opportunities.summary: François Schneider Foundation: Contemporary Talents Competition ‘Earth’ First Edition (France) Deadline: 23 Aug 2026
opportunities.details: François Schneider Foundation: Contemporary Talents Competition ‘Earth’ First Edition (France) Read this call in: French , German The François Schneider Foundation, located in Wattwiller (Alsace, France), is calling for applications for its newly launched contemporary art competition Contemporary Talents Competition with the theme ‘Earth’. Echoing the Water theme developed in Wattwiller, the François Schneider Foundation addresses the theme of Earth in a new competition held at the Pontigny Abbey estate in Burgundy. This subject is deeply linked to the history of the site, which will house a new contemporary art centre in the coming years. This first edition is open to sculptures and installations designed for outdoor display. The winning four to five artworks will form an initial artistic trail in the gardens of Pontigny Abbey, running alongside the renovation phase of the Domaine des Arts et de la Terre (2026–2028). Eligible artistic disciplines include sculpture and installation, and artists can be of any nationality. The prize is 15,000 EUR per winner for the acquisition of their artwork by the Foundation (or 8,000 EUR if the sculpture or installation has multiple editions). There will be an exhibition in spring 2027 of the winning artworks in the gardens of Pontigny Abbey, and the Foundation will cover all transportation cost of the artists for their travel to the exhibition and all the travel and insurance costs for the artworks. Deadline: 23 August 2026 More info & …

opportunities.summary: Fondation d'entreprise Martell: ‘Creation and Transitions’ Residency 2026–2027 (France) Deadline: 23 Aug 2026
opportunities.details: Fondation d'entreprise Martell: ‘Creation and Transitions’ Residency 2026–2027 (France) Read this call in: French The Fondation d’entreprise Martell is launching a new call for projects to host designers, artists, architects, curators, writers and researchers in the humanities and social sciences for research-experimentation, production and writing-curation residencies in Cognac, France, in 2026 and 2027. Open to all nationalities and levels of experience, from the emerging to the established, the programme actively encourages interdisciplinary approaches. Residency fellowships: Research and experimentation (6 – 8 weeks): This residency area concerns all projects in the conception, research, or prototyping phase. Production (2 – 6 weeks): This residency area allows residents to give shape to their ideas and produce new objects. For exhibition projects, it is also possible to apply for this area in collaboration with a partner institution. Writing and curatorship (2 – 4 weeks, during the summer): This residency area is for writers, curators, critics, and scholars in the humanities and social sciences who require space and time during the summer in the Charentes region to carry out a writing project of a literary, artistic, critical, or theoretical nature. Support: Housing Meals Transportation: coverage of one round-trip ticket between the resident’s home and the Foundation for each residency period, within the limit of two round trips within France (for a maximum of 500 EUR) …

Participants will stay at ZA-KOENJI Public Theatre for approximately two weeks, bringing their own artistic practices and research questions while engaging in collective learning, discussion, and experimentation. Held under the official auspices of the Embassy of Greece in Spain and the Municipality of Athens, this initiative explores the raw, dynamic, and poetic connections between two iconic Mediterranean capitals. ABOUT THE PROJECT Metropolises are living organisms, shaped by history, continuous movement, human encounters, and spatial evolution. "The Energy of the Metropolis" seeks to map the shared urban soul and distinct rhythms of Athens and Barcelona. Through visual storytelling, participating artists will contribute to an evolving cross-border conversation on how we inhabit, experience, and reimagine the modern city. opportunities.details: Chalk Hill offers a unique opportunity to work independently on a beautiful ranch in Sonoma County. It’s your time and space to dedicate to your work. We host one artist at a time, giving you complete access to our 1925 rustic farmhouse and dedicated studio space in a repurposed barn. The property features oak woodlands, hiking trails, vineyards, and private access to the Russian River. Artists are given the opportunity to display and sell their work at our seasonal open studios. Duration of residency 2-4 weeks Accommodation The Residency’s 1925 rustic farmhouse has three bedrooms, one shared bathroom, a kitchen, and living space. The residency is located at Warnecke Ranch & Vineyard which is a working vineyard in a rural area. We typically host one artist at a time. Sonoma County weather is beautiful year-round, but summer can be hot and dry, and winter can be cold and rainy. Chalk Hill Residency supports artists living with disabilities and mental health challenges to the best of our ability. Please inquire about special living needs, for example, attending the residency with a care provider. Artists are financially responsible for their food. Grocery stores are located in Windsor and Healdsburg, both a 15-minute drive from the Residency. The residence does not have internet access. Internet is available at our office a short walk away. Transportation to and from the Ranch is the responsibility of the artist. Photos of the residency house, 260 acre ranch, and studio space …

opportunities.summary: Solar Punk Cambodia 2026 Open Calls deadline: 31 Aug 2026
opportunities.details: Solar Punk Cambodia 2026 Solar Punk Cambodia is calling for Southeast Asian artists to submit digital artworks for a group exhibition in September 2026. Solar Punk Cambodia is a collective of doers and dreamers, artists and neighbours, aligned with the global Solarpunk movement. Guided by active hope, they focus on re-imagining and co-creating a regenerative society where community resilience and planetary health thrive together. After the launch of Solarpunk Cambodia in 2025, this year they are focusing on one key question: How could we reset and reframe what resilience means? There is a lot of discussion about the importance of being resilient in uncertain times, but how could people reconnect and rebuild society in ways beyond bouncing back to the status quo, where it's always the same ones who bear the cost of the shocks we don't control? Solar Punk Cambodia is looking for any type of art for various open calls: from illustration to digital, paintings to sculptures, interactive 3D trippy stuff to music or performances. However, for Southeast Asian artists they are looking mainly for digital art. Solar Punk Cambodia 2026 application guidelines Deadline: 31 August 2026

opportunities.details: CALL TO ARTISTS FOR A VIRTUAL RESIDENCY Architecture & Collage A four-week, virtual/online collage artist residency in August & September 2026 Final Deadline to Apply: Tuesday, 28 July 2026 Submit your application HERE Kolaj LIVE Online: Architecture and Collage Tuesday, 21 July 2026, 7-9PM EDT (2300 UTC) GET TICKETS (Free, a good opportunity to learn about the program) THESIS Kolaj Institute’s Architecture & Collage Project views Architecture as a building technology; as a form of visual art; and as culture. In this sense, a building can be a vessel of history or a site of storytelling and folklore. Buildings exist in time; their meaning and function may be different in the past, present, and future; and they exist in a dynamic cycle of construction, use, decay, preservation, reuse, and ultimately destruction. The project holds space for those buildings that are cultural symbols and works of art and those buildings that make up our neighborhoods and communities. Collage and modern architecture share a closely connected history. In the early twentieth century, as mass printing, photography, advertising, and illustrated magazines became increasingly accessible, artists and designers began cutting, combining, and recontextualizing printed images as a way to imagine new realities. opportunities.title: Open Call: Case Studies at the intersection of Arte Útil and Technology Apply now until September 6, 2026
opportunities.summary: Open Call: Case Studies at the intersection of Arte Útil and Technology Apply now until September 6, 2026
opportunities.details: Arte Útil has to do with understanding that art, only as a proposal, is not enough. Arte Útil goes from the state of proposal to that of real implementation. It has to do with understanding that proposals coming from art must reveal the next step and be applied, must leave the sphere of what is unattainable, of desired impossibility, to be part of what exists, of the real and functional sphere: to be a feasible utopia. – Tania Bruguera, reflections on Arte Útil, in “What’s the Use,” Valiz, Amsterdam, 2016 Arte Útil roughly translates as “useful art.” But it goes further, meaning art that operates beyond representation, as a tool or device to effect reality through social change. At the core of this research is an open-source archive maintained by the Asociación de Arte Útil. This growing database comprises almost three hundred case studies, from 1827 to today, describing projects that imagine, create, and implement tactics that foster civic engagement and re-evaluate institutions to make them work for the people. Application Process We are inviting the public to submit information on historical as well as ongoing projects, operating in the intersection of art and technology – thinking about how technologies can serve societies, politics and science in a spirit of conviviality and solidary coexistence. Considering that technologies are embedded in our societal cosmos, there is no single technological solution to global problems. In this sense, we are welcoming a broad …

opportunities.requirements: CV, Portfolio, Project proposal, Motivation letter
opportunities.details: The Embassy of Foreign Artists residency programme is partnering with the Centre for Digital Humanities and Multilateralism at the Geneva Graduate Institute to offer a three-month artist residency to conduct archival research in the heart of international organisations based in Geneva, Switzerland. The archives of international organisations in Geneva form part of humanity’s collective memory. While these fragments constitute a formal record comprising reports, official correspondence, international agreements, speeches, and documentary images of a select few, they nonetheless contain the narratives of millions of human stories. Multilateral histories can also be discerned through handwritten notes, draft reports, unofficial maps, artworks, informal sound recordings, and absences. Seen through the eyes of artists and researchers, this residency aims to transform this material and give it a new dimension. Applicants are invited to propose projects that develop novel perspectives on topics such as: (un)told human stories; intergovernmental decision making processes; multilateral successes and failures; and reimagined visions for the future of international cooperation. Applications must relate to projects that use the archives of Geneva-based international intergovernmental or non-governmental organisations as their primary resource (such as UN Archives Geneva, the International Committee of the Red Cross Archives, etc.). Projects may, however, have links with other …

opportunities.title: The promise of the creatures vol thinking ourselves as birds artistic and zoological practices for other versions of the world
opportunities.details: Coordinator: Celeste Medrano Bipedal locomotion, a presumably biological arrangement, brought with it a series of political consequences that, among certain human collectives, meant an overt opening toward all kinds of binary thinking. Thus, far from the ground, we found ourselves in the midst of a taxonomic whim. However, playing the exceptionalism card did not make us “win the game,” as we had imagined. Today we must think of ourselves amid all kinds of catastrophes: anthropocenic, denialist, libertarian, etc. But: how can we engage in an exercise that moves away from the simplifications proposed by Modernity? What paths can we take toward more-than-human futures? Perhaps here we can conjure a promise: that of the critters. In this re(in)sidency, the second version of an essay we began in 2025, we slip into the world of birds as a multispecies pretext. We imagine the gathering as an act of resistance to the progress of a technocratic and libertarian linear time; we imagine it chiefly inhabited by legs and beaks, by the feathers of male birds, female birds, and aviaries. We imagine it relapsing into critterhood, insisting. Flying over the coastal grasslands of Buenos Aires Province, dragging ourselves through the forest that surrounds them. For all this, it is necessary to learn certain techniques—perhaps the biological ones, those of naturalists and ornithologists—in pursuit of other possible stories. opportunities.summary: 2026 FINNO-UGRIC CREATIVE RESIDENCY IN NARVA Narva Art Residency (NART), in collaboration with the Estonian Academy of Arts, is inviting applications for the 2026 Finno-Ugric Creative Residency, taking place 27 November–6 December 2026. The programme supports artists with roots in or strong connections to Finno-Ugric peoples, and aims to strengthen and celebrate Finno-Ugric cultural identities thr
opportunities.details: Narva Art Residency announces an open call for a Finno-Ugric creative residency, which will take place in late 2026. It is organised in collaboration with the Department of Fashion Design of the Estonian Academy of Arts. NART hosted the first edition of the Finno-Ugric creative residency in 2025 as part of the Narva Finno-Ugric Capital of Culture programme. The call was very popular, and artist Weronika Trojanska was selected to work on the topic of lament songs. It showed that art is a powerful tool for creating dialogues and strengthening cultural identity. It is important to highlight and introduce the cultures of small Finno-Ugric peoples whose identities have been continuously threatened by Russia’s actions. Many Finno-Ugric people living abroad are losing touch with their identity, and therefore, further identification and discovery are particularly important. We are looking for applications from artists and creative people with roots from or strong ties to the Finno-Ugric peoples. The call is open to various creative fields, including visual art, music, theatre, and performance. The residency comes with support from the Erasmus+ programme and is therefore directed to applicants from eligible countries (see the list here ). In 2026, the second edition of the programme will include new features. As before, the selected artist is expected to create a work inspired by Finno-Ugric cultures. opportunities.title: A $90,000 Graduate Fellowship for Immigrants & Children of Immigrants in the Visual Arts
opportunities.summary: The Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowships for New Americans supports immigrants & children of immigrants in MFA, MA, PhD & other graduate programs.
opportunities.details: The Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowships for New Americans supports immigrants and children of immigrants pursuing graduate study in the United States — including visual artists, designers, architects, and filmmakers. Each year, 30 Fellows receive up to $90,000 in funding (up to $25,000/year stipend; up to $20,000/year tuition support) for up to two years of full-time study at any accredited institution in the US. The Fellowship community spans every creative discipline — painting, printmaking, sculpture, architecture, design, film, and beyond — alongside scientists, lawyers, physicians, and public policy leaders. Fellows join a lifelong community of nearly 900 New Americans with family origins in over 100 countries. "In the architecture field or as an artist, legitimacy can feel scarce and difficult to come by. The Paul & Daisy Soros [Fellowships] provides that," says Jonathan Herrera Soto , 2023 Paul & Daisy Soros Fellow, MFA in painting & printmaking, Yale School of Art. "Being in proximity and in conversation with other immigrants and children of immigrants has been very nourishing." Selection is merit-based and holistic, emphasizing creativity, originality, initiative, and sustained accomplishment. Eligible applicants include naturalized citizens, green card holders, asylees and refugees, US-born children of two immigrant parents, and those born abroad who graduated from both high school and college in the United States. Jurors were Laura Mott, Chief Curator of Cranbrook Art Museum, Bloomfield Hills, MI; Michael Rooks, Wieland Family Senior Curator of Modern and Contemporary Art, High Museum of Art, Atlanta, GA; Edra Soto, Chicago-based artist, educator, and co-director of outdoor project space The Franklin, Chicago, IL. opportunities.details: Chloe Chiasson (The Bennett Prize Round 2 Finalist), “A New Dawn” (2021), oil, acrylic, resin, wood, and a match on canvas, 78.25 x 96 inches Aspiring women painters are invited to apply for The Bennett Prize . The newly increased $75,000 grand prize is the largest offered solely to women figurative realist painters. For the third time, an additional award of $10,000 will be given to one other finalist. The call for entries runs through September 19, 2026. See the complete rules . Dallas, Texas-based artist Amy Werntz won the fourth Bennett Prize in 2025, following winners Shiqing Deng in 2023, Ayana Ross in 2021, and Aneka Ingold in 2019. Notably, Werntz was named a finalist in the second Bennett Prize competition in 2021. She is currently creating new work for her Bennett Prize solo exhibition, which will travel the country starting next year. The exhibition will be on display during the summer of 2027 at the Muskegon Museum of Art (MMA) in Muskegon, Michigan. Endowed by art collectors Steven Alan Bennett and Dr. Elaine Melotti Schmidt at the MMA, The Bennett Prize aims to elevate women figurative realist painters—helping them achieve their full potential. The winner receives $37,500 each year for two years to create a solo show. opportunities.details: The Center for Craft is now accepting applications for the 2026 Craft Archive Fellowship , offering four $5,000 awards to support research on underrepresented craft histories in the United States. The fellowship is open to a range of scholars — from emerging to established, including independent and artist researchers — to conduct archival research on feminist, intersectional, queer, Black, Indigenous, Latinx, Asian American and Pacific Islander, and other nondominant craft histories. Fellows will have the opportunity to engage in both conventional and innovative archival research, culminating in a special feature in Hyperallergic and a virtual program hosted by the Center for Craft in September 2027. Three of the Craft Archive Fellowships will be named the Ayumi Horie Award, the Sara Clugage Award, and the Gallaher Family Award. Additional awards may be named by contacting give@centerforcraft.org . An information session will be held virtually on April 7, 2026, from 5 to 6 pm (ET). The session is free, but registration is required. Register here . opportunities.title: Frankenthaler Climate Initiative Opens Applications for Sixth Grant Cycle
opportunities.summary: The program has awarded more than $17.5 million to US visual arts organizations pursuing energy efficiency assessments and projects.
opportunities.details: The Helen Frankenthaler Foundation has opened the sixth application cycle for the Frankenthaler Climate Initiative (FCI) , reaffirming its commitment to building a more sustainable and resilient future for the visual arts. Since its launch in 2021, the program has become the largest private national grantmaking initiative of its kind, supporting visual arts organizations in the United States through assessment, planning, and implementation of efforts to reduce their environmental impact through clean energy generation and energy efficiency measures. Overseen by the Helen Frankenthaler Foundation in association with Environment & Culture Partners and Green Design Collaborative, FCI has awarded more than $17.5 million to 249 institutions across 40 states to date. “With each successive cycle, we continue to see how the arts sector is driving forward new models for sustainability,” said Elizabeth Smith, Executive Director of the Helen Frankenthaler Foundation. “Arts organizations across the country are translating their values into action, developing projects that not only improve their energy performance but also model new ways of thinking about stewardship and resourcefulness. Each cycle contributes to shaping a resilient, low-carbon cultural landscape.” Eligible organizations are invited to apply for the following grant types: Catalyst Grants provide up to $20,000 to organizations with annual operating budgets under $500,000 pursuing small-scale or first-time energy …

opportunities.title: The Rubin’s Annual Grant Program Funds Himalayan Art and Research
opportunities.summary: The 2026 grant cycle opens February 16. Submit a letter of intent by March 6.
opportunities.details: In 2024, the Rubin launched a new annual grant program to support artists, creatives, and scholars who are expanding awareness and understanding of Himalayan art globally, as well as the rich cultural legacy and living traditions of the greater Himalayan region. Over the past two years, the Rubin has supported 32 projects from around the world with grants ranging from $3,000 to $25,000, depending on the scale, impact, and needs of each proposal. The Rubin x Research grants aim to support scholars who are broadening Himalayan art research to generate further knowledge, documentation, and general awareness of the field. The Rubin x Art Projects grants support artists and creatives whose practices give visibility to the rich cultural legacy and living traditions of the Himalayan region and its power to inspire societies today. Photo by Filip Wolak, courtesy the Rubin Museum of Himalayan Art Examples of projects that have received grants include a new conservation training program in Mongolia; documentation of historic art in central Bhutan and Nepal; research that focuses on the provenance of objects from a Tibetan Buddhist temple in Darjeeling, India; Tibetan visual art teaching resources and materials for educators; a two-channel video installation in northern India that explores the Tibetan Buddhist concept of interdependence; new exhibitions, multimedia projects, and much more. opportunities.details: Aktuelles REMINDER: Ausschreibung Kalinowski-Preis 2026 12.01.2026 Die „Nachlass-Stiftung Professor Horst Egon Kalinowski“ schreibt bis zum 31. Januar 2026 den mit 10.000 Euro dotierten Kalinowski-Preis aus. Der Förderpreis richtet sich an Absolvent:innen der Staatlichen Kunstakademie Karlsruhe und wird zum 10. Mal vergeben. Der Düsseldorfer Bildhauer und Grafiker Horst Egon Kalinowski (1924-2013) gründete noch zu seinen Lebzeiten im Jahr 2011 die „Nachlass-Stiftung Professor Horst Egon Kalinowski“ . Die treuhänderisch von der Stiftung Kunstfonds verwaltete Nachlass-Stiftung hat den Zweck, das Werk Kalinowskis zu bewahren und öffentlich zugänglich zu machen, u.a. im Rahmen von Ausstellungen und wissenschaftlicher Forschung. Darüber hinaus hat Kalinowski in seinem Testament verfügt, dass seine Nachlass-Stiftung aus ihren Erträgen einen Förderpreis für Absolvent:innen der Staatlichen Kunstakademie Karlsruhe auslobt, an der er selbst von 1972 bis zu seiner Emeritierung 1989 lehrte. Für den Förderpreis bewerben können sich ausschließlich Absolvent:innen der Staatlichen Akademie der Bildenden Künste Karlsruhe, deren Abschluss (Diplom) nicht länger als zehn Jahre zurückliegt. Bewerbungsschluss ist der 31. Januar 2026 (24 Uhr) . Die Antragstellung erfolgt online über das Bewerbungsportal der Stiftung Kunstfonds. Die Juryentscheidung fällt voraussichtlich im April 2026. opportunities.details: Aktuelles REMINDER AUSSCHREIBUNG: Kalinowski-Preis 2024 02.01.2024 Die „Nachlass-Stiftung Professor Horst Egon Kalinowski“ schreibt den mit 10.000 Euro dotierten Kalinowski-Preis aus. Der Förderpreis richtet sich an Absolvent:innen der Staatlichen Kunstakademie Karlsruhe und wird zum 8. Mal vergeben. Der Düsseldorfer Bildhauer und Grafiker Horst Egon Kalinowski (1924-2013) gründete noch zu seinen Lebzeiten im Jahr 2011 die „Nachlass-Stiftung Professor Horst Egon Kalinowski“ . Die treuhänderisch von der Stiftung Kunstfonds verwaltete Nachlass-Stiftung hat den Zweck, das Werk Kalinowskis zu bewahren und öffentlich zugänglich zu machen, u.a. im Rahmen von Ausstellungen und wissenschaftlicher Forschung. Darüber hinaus hat Kalinowski in seinem Testament verfügt, dass seine Nachlass-Stiftung aus ihren Erträgen einen Förderpreis für Absolvent:innen der Staatlichen Kunstakademie Karlsruhe auslobt, an der er selbst von 1972 bis zu seiner Emeritierung 1989 lehrte. Für den Förderpreis bewerben können sich ausschließlich Absolvent:innen der Staatlichen Akademie der Bildenden Künste Karlsruhe, deren Abschluss (Diplom) nicht länger als zehn Jahre zurückliegt. Bewerbungsschluss ist der 31. Januar 2024 (24 Uhr) . Die Fördergrundsätze und Hinweise zur Antragstellung finden Sie hier , direkt zur Antragstellung gelangen Sie hier . Vor diesem Hintergrund liegen in den Sonderförderprogrammen „NEUSTARTplus-Stipendium“ und „NEUSTARTplus Plattformen der bildenden Kunst“ bisher keine abgeschlossenen Listen der Geförderten vor. Fachjurys und Stiftung Kunstfonds haben zum Ziel, die Geförderten beider NEUSTARTplus-Programme bis Mitte Dezember 2022 final bekanntgeben zu können. Über die Förderungen entscheiden das Kuratorium und die Kommission für das Sonderförderprogramm 20/21 NEUSTART KULTUR. Die Jurys sind unabhängig und mehrheitlich mit bildenden Künstler:innen besetzt. Die Stiftung Kunstfonds hat mit der Förderlinie NEUSTARTplus zwei Sonderförderprogramme ausgeschrieben, die Pilotcharakter haben: Mit ihnen soll freischaffenden bildenden Künstler:innen bzw. Ausstellungsorten der Kunstszene ein nachhaltiger Neustart in 2023 ermöglicht werden. Die Erkenntnisse aus der Durchführung der Programme sind zudem Basis für eine Neuausrichtung der regulären Kunstfonds-Förderprogramme ab 2024. opportunities.details: Aktuelles REMINDER – AUSSCHREIBUNG NEUSTARTplus-Stipendium für bildende Künstler:innen 18.08.2022 Pressemitteilung. Die Stiftung Kunstfonds schreibt 550 Halbjahresstipendien für freiberuflich tätige bildende Künstler:innen in Höhe von je 18.000 Euro aus. Das „Sonderförderprogramm NEUSTARTplus-Stipendium“ will bildenden Künstler:innen ein konzentriertes Arbeiten ermöglichen sowie ihnen den Freiraum geben, eine nachhaltige Basis für das weitere künstlerische Schaffen aufzubauen bzw. zu stärken. Antragsberechtigt sind bildende Künstler:innen, die solo-selbstständig und freischaffend tätig sind, dauerhaft in Deutschland leben und nicht immatrikuliert sind. Bewerber:innen dürfen nicht angestellt sein, eine geringfügige Beschäftigung („Minijob“) ist jedoch zulässig. Auch Künstler:innen-Duos können sich bewerben. Das Stipendium wird über einen Förderzeitraum von sechs Monaten vom 1. Januar 2023 bis zum 30. Juni 2023 ausbezahlt. Bewerbungsschluss ist der 15. September 2022 (24 Uhr). Die Antragstellung ist ausschließlich online möglich über das Bewerbungsportal der Stiftung Kunstfonds auf bewerbung.kunstfonds.de . Die Stiftung Kunstfonds unterstützt mit dem Sonderförderprogramm „NEUSTARTplus Plattformen der bildenden Kunst“ Einrichtungen und Orte, die zeitgenössische bildende Kunst präsentieren, vermitteln und am aktuellen Diskurs teilnehmen. Ziel ist es, diese in ihrer Funktion als analoge Plattformen für Innovation und Austausch zu stärken. Antragsberechtigt sind z.B. Kunst- und Atelierhäuser, Produzent:innengalerien, Kunstvereine, Galerien, Künstler:innenkollektive oder freie Kunstorte. Sie müssen ihren Sitz in Deutschland haben und mit ihren Aktivitäten eine überregionale Wirkung erzielen. Gefördert werden komplexe, auch mehrmonatig konzipierte Projektvorhaben, die z.B. Ausstellungen, Symposien oder alternative analoge Formate beinhalten. Förderfähig sind hierbei alle Maßnahmen, die zur Umsetzung und Vermittlung erforderlich sind, also auch Vor- und Nachbereitungen oder Recherchen. Der Förderzeitraum beginnt am 1. Januar 2023 und endet am 30.Juni 2023. Die Höchstfördersumme beträgt 70.000 Euro, die Mindestantragssumme 10.000 Euro. Ein Eigenanteil von 10 Prozent ist erforderlich. Bewerbungsschluss ist der 15. opportunities.details: Aktuelles REMINDER – AUSSCHREIBUNG Sonderförderprogramm: Residenzen für bildende Künstler:innen aus der Ukraine 18.08.2022 Pressemitteilung. Die Stiftung Kunstfonds setzt ein „Sonderförderprogramm Ukraine“ in Höhe von 500.000 Euro um. Die Mittel stammen aus dem vom Deutschen Bundestag bewilligten Sonderhaushalt „Ukraine“. Ziel des Sonderförderprogrammes ist es, bildende Künstler:innen, die aufgrund des aktuellen Kriegsgeschehens aus der Ukraine nach Deutschland geflüchtet sind und nun hier Wohn- und Arbeitsmöglichkeiten benötigen, zu unterstützen. Einrichtungen, die für diese Künstler:innen Residenzen anbieten, sollen in ihrem Engagement gestärkt werden. Antragsberechtigt sind daher Künstlerhäuser, Atelierhäuser, Kunstvereine, Kommunen und Einrichtungen des Kunstbetriebs, die in Deutschland Unterkunft und Arbeitsmöglichkeit - sog. Residenzen - für seit Kriegsbeginn aus der Ukraine geflüchtete bildende Künstler:innen zur Verfügung stellen. Die geförderten Einrichtungen erhalten eine monatliche Pauschale von bis zu 1.000 Euro für künstlerische Betreuung und Betriebskosten. Zusätzlich erhalten die Residenz-Künstler:innen ein monatliches Stipendium von je 1.500 Euro, das über die Einrichtungen ausgezahlt wird. Die Auswahl der Künstler:innen sowie die Antragstellung für Stipendien und Monatspauschalen erfolgt über die Einrichtungen. Der Bewerbungsschluss ist der 31. August 2022 (24 Uhr). Stiftung Kunstfonds vergibt in ihrem regulären Förderprogramm 70 Arbeitsstipendien für bildende Künstler:innen und fördert neun künstlerische Projektvorhaben. Die jährlich mit Einreichfrist zum 31. Oktober ausgeschriebenen Arbeitsstipendien der Stiftung Kunstfonds haben eine Laufzeit von 12 Monaten, sind mit jeweils 22.000 Euro dotiert und werden in festen Monatsraten ausbezahlt. Sie haben zum Ziel, als eine Art Kreativ-Booster zu wirken und bildenden Künstler:innen ein freies, auf die Kunst konzentriertes Arbeiten zu ermöglichen. Die Stipendien sind dabei weder ortsgebunden noch altersbegrenzt. Sie richten sich an erfahrene Künstler:innen wie auch an jene, die am Anfang ihrer Karriere stehen. Mit ihrer konkreten Ausrichtung auf die Bedarfe von bildenden Künstler:innen sind die Arbeitsstipendien der Stiftung Kunstfonds ein in der bundesweiten Kunstszene unerlässliches Förderinstrument. Insgesamt vergibt die Stiftung Kunstfonds 70 Stipendien mit einer Gesamtfördersumme von 1,54 Mio. Euro. Die regulär für Arbeitsstipendien zur Verfügung stehenden Stiftungsmittel wurden mithilfe von NEUSTART KULTUR-Geldern der Bundesregierung um 1 Mio. Euro aufgestockt. Außerdem werden neun künstlerische Projekte mit einer Gesamtfördersumme von 163.400 Euro unterstützt. Diese Förderung gibt bildenden Künstler:innen die Chance, konkrete Vorhaben zu realisieren. opportunities.details: Aktuelles REMINDER: Ausschreibung Kalinowski-Preis 2022 10.01.2022 Absolvent:innen der Staatlichen Akademie der Bildenden Künste Karlsruhe können sich bis zum 31. Januar um die renommierte Auszeichnung bewerben. Der Düsseldorfer Bildhauer und Grafiker Horst Egon Kalinowski (1924-2013) gründete noch zu seinen Lebzeiten im Jahr 2011 die „Nachlass-Stiftung Professor Horst Egon Kalinowski“ . Die treuhänderisch von der Stiftung Kunstfonds verwaltete Nachlass-Stiftung hat den Zweck, das Werk Kalinowskis zu bewahren und öffentlich zugänglich zu machen, u.a. im Rahmen von Ausstellungen und wissenschaftlicher Forschung. Darüber hinaus hat Kalinowski in seinem Testament verfügt, dass seine Nachlass-Stiftung aus ihren Erträgen einen Förderpreis für Absolvent:innen der Staatlichen Kunstakademie Karlsruhe auslobt, an der er selbst von 1972 bis zu seiner Emeritierung 1989 lehrte. Die „Nachlass-Stiftung Professor Horst Egon Kalinowski“ schreibt den mit 10.000 Euro dotierten Kalinowski-Preis zum sechsten Mal aus. Bewerben können sich ausschließlich Absolvent:innen der Staatlichen Akademie der Bildenden Künste Karlsruhe, deren Abschluss (Diplom) nicht länger als zehn Jahre zurückliegt. Bewerbungsschluss ist der 31. Januar 2022 . Die Fördergrundsätze und Hinweise zur Antragstellung finden Sie hier , direkt zur Antragstellung gelangen Sie hier . opportunities.details: Aktuelles Änderung der Ausschreibung für Werkverzeichnungen in 2021 05.02.2021 Bewerbungen können nur digital eingereicht werden Die aktuelle Corona-Schutzverordnung erfordert es, dass wir unser laufendes Ausschreibungsverfahren zur Förderung von Werkverzeichnungen anpassen: Ab jetzt können Bewerbungen nur noch digital eingereicht werden. Der Grund dafür ist, dass uns Corona ein persönliches Zusammentreffen der Vergabejury jetzt und in naher Zukunft nicht erlaubt. Dies macht auch eine Beurteilung von analogen Dokumentationsmaterialien unmöglich. Die Jurysitzung wird aber als virtuelle Konferenz stattfinden, denn uns ist es wichtig das Verfahren zu einem Ergebnis zu bringen. Bewerber*innen können das Online-Antragssystem des Kunstfonds auf bewerbung.kunstfonds.de nutzen: Hier einfach das Online-Formular digital ausfüllen und einreichen. Im Online- Formular haben Sie die Möglichkeit, Werkbeispiele hochzuladen. Wir bitten Sie, mindestens 10 bzw. maximal 30 Werkbeispiele als Jpeg-Datei und in einer Größe von je maximal 500 KB einzureichen. Medienkünstler*innen können einen Vimeo-Link zu einem Werkbeispiel oder einen Zusammenschnitt mit einer Gesamtlänge von max. 10 Minuten abgeben. Bitte senden Sie uns keine analogen Antragsunterlagen und keine Anträge per E-Mail. Alle weiteren Informationen zur Ausschreibung finden Sie hier . opportunities.details: Aktuelles KALINOWSKI-PREIS 2021 15.01.2021 Ausschreibung der Nachlass-Stiftung Prof. Horst Egon Kalinowski Horst Egon Kalinowski (1924-2013), Düsseldorfer Bildhauer und Grafiker, gründete noch zu Lebzeiten im Jahr 2011 die „Nachlass-Stiftung Professor Horst Egon Kalinowski“ . Die treuhänderisch von der Stiftung Kunstfonds verwaltete Nachlass-Stiftung hat den Zweck, das Oeuvre Kalinowskis zu bewahren und öffentlich zugänglich zu machen. Die Werke Kalinowskis stehen für Ausstellungen und wissenschaftliche Forschungen zur Verfügung. Darüber hinaus hat Kalinowski in seinem Testament verfügt, dass seine Nachlass-Stiftung aus ihren Erträgen einen Förderpreis für Absolvent*innen der Staatlichen Kunstakademie Karlsruhe auslobt, an der er selbst von 1972 bis zu seiner Emeritierung in 1989 lehrte. Die „Nachlass-Stiftung Professor Horst Egon Kalinowski“ schreibt zum fünften Mal den mit 10.000 Euro dotierten KALINOWSKI-PREIS aus. Bewerben können sich ausschließlich Absolvent*innen der Staatlichen Akademie der Bildenden Künste Karlsruhe. Bewerbungsschluss ist der 31. Januar 2021 . Künstler*innen, kunstvermittelnde Akteure und Institutionen haben 1209 Projekte zur Förderung vorgeschlagen. Schon jetzt ist abzusehen, dass die für diesen dritten Teil des Programms zur Verfügung stehenden 3 Mio. Euro bei weitem nicht ausreichen, um den dringenden Bedarf der Szene zu decken. Bereits am 10. September war die Deadline für das mit je 9.000 Euro dotierte halbjährliche Stipendium, für das sich 4776 bildende Künstler*innen bewerben. Die Förderquote wird, wie schon beim Stipendium für Künstler*innen mit Kindern unter 7 Jahren, dem ersten Programmteil, auch hier bei ca. 11,5 % liegen, da die zur Verfügung stehenden 5 Mio. Euro nur für 550 Stipendien ausreichen. Die 16-köpfige Jury wird alle Anträge in den nächsten Wochen sorgfältig prüfen und über eine Förderung entscheiden. Wegen der vielen Bewerbungen wird sich die Juryzeit verlängern, die Entscheidung über die Stipendien voraussichtlich erst Mitte Oktober bzw. über die Projektförderungen voraussichtlich erst Mitte November fallen. 09. opportunities.details: Aktuelles Programm „Stipendium für Künstler*innen mit Kindern unter 7 Jahren“ zehnfach überzeichnet 10.08.2020 Am 6. August 2020 endete die Einreichfrist für die erste Ausschreibung des Sonderförderprogramms 20/21, das durch das von der Beauftragten der Bundesregierung für Kultur und Medien initiierte Hilfspaket NEUSTART KULTUR ermöglicht wurde. Das erste Förderprogramm richtete sich an in Deutschland lebende zeitgenössische bildende Künstler*innen mit Kindern unter 7 Jahren, die freischaffend bzw. solo-selbstständig tätig sind. Sie trifft die Krise besonders hart, da sie neben dem Wegfall ihrer Einkommen auch Kleinkinder im Vorschulalter zu betreuen haben. Ein künstlerisches Arbeiten unter diesen Bedingungen ist nur schwer möglich. Die 849 eingegangen Anträge auf ein Stipendium für Künstler*innen mit Kindern unter 7 Jahren zeugen von der Notwendigkeit und Dringlichkeit der sofortigen Hilfe für diese Zielgruppe. Das mit 12.000 Euro dotierte halbjährliche Stipendium soll bereits ab September von der Stiftung Kunstfonds an die Künstler*innen ausbezahlt werden. Eine 16-köpfige Fachjury wird in den kommenden 3 Wochen über die Anträge entscheiden und rund 80 Stipendien vergeben. Zwei weitere Förderprogramme des Sonderprogramms 20/21 starten in dieser Woche; das erste ebenfalls in Form eines Stipendiums, das sich an in Deutschland lebende freischaffende, solo-selbständige bildende Künstler*innen wendet und ein zweites, das eine Projektförderung für kunstvermittelnde Akteure (z. opportunities.summary: 04. November 2019 AUSSCHREIBUNG – KALINOWSKI-PREIS der Nachlass-Stiftung Prof. Horst Egon Kalinowski
opportunities.details: Aktuelles AUSSCHREIBUNG – KALINOWSKI-PREIS 04.11.2019 der Nachlass-Stiftung Prof. Horst Egon Kalinowski Horst Egon Kalinowski (1924-2013), Düsseldorfer Bildhauer und Grafiker, gründete noch zu Lebzeiten im Jahr 2011 die „Nachlass-Stiftung Professor Horst Egon Kalinowski“. Die treuhänderisch von der Stiftung Kunstfonds verwaltete Nachlass-Stiftung hat den Zweck, das Oeuvre Kalinowskis zu bewahren und öffentlich zugänglich zu machen. Die Werke Kalinowskis stehen für Ausstellungen und wissenschaftliche Forschungen zur Verfügung. Darüber hinaus hat Kalinowski in seinem Testament verfügt, dass seine Nachlass-Stiftung aus ihren Erträgen einen Förderpreis für Absolventen der Staatlichen Kunstakademie Karlsruhe, an der er selbst von 1972 bis zu seiner Emeritierung 1989 lehrte, auslobt. Die „Nachlass-Stiftung Professor Horst Egon Kalinowski“ schreibt zum vierten Mal den mit 10.000 Euro dotierten KALINOWSKI-PREIS aus. Bewerben können sich ausschließlich Absolventen der Staatlichen Akademie der Bildenden Künste Karlsruhe. Bewerbungsschluss ist der 31. Januar 2020. opportunities.title: Site specific sponsored residencies in venice for artists writers and researchers create and present in the heart of the venetian ghetto
opportunities.details: Open Call for Artists, writers, researchers across disciplines to Live Create and present/exhibit their work in the heart of the Venetian Ghetto Deadline: 31.07. 2026 Venezia Contemporanea, in cooperation with Galleria ScalaMata Space in Venice, Italy, are offering a partly and fully covered residencies. Located at the heart of the picturesque historic Jewish Ghetto of Venice – the first Ghetto in Europe, established in 1516 – We welcome Jewish and non-Jewish artists, writers, and researchers across all disciplines to live, create and present their work. The La-Storta and Skyline are located in two historic buildings in the heart of Venice’s vibrant, ancient Ghetto. We offer residencies that immerse artists in an authentic Venetian serene and vivid atmosphere. The main bars and restaurants hub is just across the bridge. Vaporetto station is just around the corner. The supermarket is within walking distance. The bus station Piazzale Roma and train station Ferrovia Santa Lucia and supermarket are within walking distance. Temporal laboratory situated practices in the environment
opportunities.details: Laboratorio Temporal (Temporal Laboratory) is an ongoing, transdisciplinary residency program that invites artists, researchers, writers, and scientists to suspend the rhythm of major cities and engage in a situated practice. Located in the unique, semi-rural environment of El Marquesado (where forest, dunes, cliffs, and sea converge), the residency aims to dismantle extractivist logics of fast consumption and production. Grounded in the material turn, our goal is to foster projects that treat the territory, its matter, and its biological cycles not as a passive backdrop, but as active co-producers of meaning and memory. Programming & Structure The residency rejects rigid structures. Instead of fixed dates, we offer a highly flexible format where the duration and timing of each stay are co-designed with the residents on a rolling basis to match the needs of their research and the seasonal shifts of the environment. Programming includes critical accompaniment and mentorship by the founders, field support through alliances with scientific institutions (such as Fundación Azara), and the opportunity to activate processes locally through community-engaged formats like Open Studios, shared walks, workshops, or archive activations. Conditions & Workspace Residents live and work in an outstanding 100 m² wood architectural structure, featuring a large communal hall for collective thinking, private mezzanine workspaces, a shared kitchen, and direct access to the surrounding landscape. …
