opportunities.details: The trace is an ambivalent form of inscription: it marks the presence of what once was and, at the same time, signals its absence. It is testimony and emptiness, memory and projection. From this tension, the territory presents itself as a space where human presence, natural processes and collective imaginaries are in contant dialogue. These residencies are framed within the concepts of body, territory and spatiality, understood as central axes of research and creation. In this edition, we would like to place special emphasis on the trace as a notion that cuts across these frameworks, inviting participants to explore it from multiple dimensions. However, this proposal will not be exclusive, but will remain open to projects that engage in a broad dialogue with the programme’s curatorial lines. AADK Spain invites artists and researchers to participate in this edition of artistic residencies, aimed at exploring the notion of the trace as a place of transition between presence and absence, and as a tool for reconfiguring the relationship between space and memory. Participants are invited to think of the footprint as a material record and as an ephemeral gesture capable of expanding the ways of inhabiting and signifying the territory. opportunities.details: The Expanded Photography Research Residency is a hybrid international program organized by FotoCreativaBA in collaboration with IDEA R LAB (directed by Hiroko Ohtsuki in Kurashiki, Japan). The platform connects expanded photography, visual observation, material processes, local contexts, and global cultural exchange. The programming is structured into three distinct phases: Phase 1 (12-Month Online Laboratory): Shifting away from heavy weekly screen time, this phase prioritizes autonomous processes, deep reading, and monthly theoretical/creative triggers linking contemporary expanded photography with Japanese aesthetics (e.g., Wabi-Sabi, Kintsugi, the Ma interval, and the Provoke movement). It includes monthly 1-on-1 curatorial reviews, collective critiques, and guest lectures. Phase 2 (1-Month On-Site Residency): Fieldwork at IDEA R LAB focused on studio work, site-specific research, and material investigation using local industrial waste. Phase 3 (Closing & Public Presentation): Final project reviews, open studios, process-based exhibitions, or activations both online and at the FotoCreativaBA gallery. The program is explicitly conceived as a space for exploration, learning, and transcultural dialogue rather than a purely production-oriented residency. opportunities.title: Initiative Musik — Strukturförderung
opportunities.summary: Strukturförderung
opportunities.details: Strukturförderung Programmbeschreibung FAQ Zum Antrag Die Strukturförderung dient dem Aufbau nachhaltiger professioneller Strukturen und Rahmenbedingungen im Bereich Popularmusik und Jazz am Standort Deutschland. Das Programm unterstützt Transformationsprozesse sowie Diskurse und Vernetzung in der Musikwirtschaft. Zudem sollen in enger Zusammenarbeit mit Ländern und Kommunen regionale wie länderspezifische Fördereinrichtungen und Netzwerke für Popularmusik und Jazz entwickelt, aufgebaut und gestärkt werden. Das Förderprogramm konzentriert sich gleichermaßen auf dialogische Netzwerkveranstaltungen wie Konferenzen und Conventions für die Musikbranche, als auch auf qualifizierende Formate für alle Akteur:innen der Pop-, Jazz-, und Livekultur, z.B. durch Workshopreihen und Mentoringprogramme. Auch wissenschaftliche Studien und Evaluationen zur Popkultur und Musikwirtschaft in Deutschland können gefördert werden. In unserer Doku sind alle Förderungen seit 2020 auf einen Blick ersichtlich. Für die Antragstellung empfehlen wir außerdem unsere Schritt-für-Schritt-Anleitung durch das Antragstool . opportunities.title: Initiative Musik — Exportförderung
opportunities.summary: Exportförderung
opportunities.details: Exportförderung Mit unseren Exportprogrammen und -projekten fördern wir sowohl Musiker:innen als auch Musikunternehmen bei der Verbreitung ihres Re pertoires im Ausland. Im Rahmen unserer Internationalen Live- und Showcaseförderung können Musiker:innen finanzielle Unterstützung für Auftritte im Ausland beantragen. Das Programm Internationale Exportförderung für Musikunternehmen unterstützt kleine und mittlere Unternehmen sowie Einzelunternehmer:innen der Musikwirtschaft beim Ausbau ihrer interna tionalen Aktivitäten zur Positionierung ihrer deutschen Acts. Internationale Exportförderung für Musikunternehmen Programmbeschreibung FAQ Zum Antrag Ziel des Programms Internationale Exportförderung für Musikunternehmen ist es, die internationale Wettbewerbsfähigkeit von Musikunternehmen mit Sitz in Deutschland nachhaltig zu stärken. Dies geschieht sowohl durch eigeninitiierte Maßnahmen als auch durch die Teilnahme an internationalen Branchenveranstaltungen. Das Programm ermöglicht es den Unternehmen, neue Märkte zu erschließen, nachhaltige Kontakte und Netzwerke aufzubauen und ihre deutschen Acts international zu positionieren. Priorisiert werden Veranstaltungen in Zielländern, in denen das Unternehmen und/oder die Künstler:innen bisher nicht oder in nicht ausreichendem Maße vertreten sind, aber bereits eine Followerschaft oder Kontakte über Agent:innen, Managements oder soziale Medien nachweisen können. opportunities.title: Initiative Musik — Livemusikförderung
opportunities.summary: Livemusikförderung
opportunities.details: Livemusikförderung Mit unserer Livemusikförderung wollen wir durch verschiedene Auftrittsorte die Infrastruktur der vielfältigen deutschen Musiklandschaft unterstützen. Das Programm Live 500 richtet sich an Musikclubs und regionale Veranstalter:innen von kleineren Konzerten und Konzertformaten mit Newcomer:innen oder experimentellen Genres. Mit dem Festivalförderfonds werden Musikfestivals unterstützt, die besondere soziokulturelle Schwerpunkte setzen etwa in der Nachwuchsförderung, durch eine anspruchsvolle Programmplanung oder Engagement für ökologische Nachhaltigkeit. Das Förderprogramm PlugIn unterstützt Livemusikspielstätten bei der Verbesserung ihrer technischen Ausstattung in auftrittsrelevanten Bereichen. Live 500 Programmbeschreibung FAQ Zum Antrag In der aktuellen wirtschaftlich angespannten Situation setzen viele Livemusikspielstätten und Veranstalter:innen verstärkt auf etablierte Musiker:innen. Konzertformate mit Newcomer:innen, weniger populäre oder experimentelle Genres laufen dabei Gefahr zu sehr in den Hintergrund zu treten. Das aufgelegte Förderprogramm Live 500 III soll hier ansetzen. Es soll ein Fortbestehen der kulturellen Vielfalt an Livemusikprogrammen sichern. Darüber hinaus zielt es darauf ab, die Musikspielstätten und Veranstalter:innen bei einer diverseren Programmplanung und faireren Vergütungen der Künstler:innen zu unterstützen und somit mehr kulturelle Teilhabe für Künstler:innen zu ermöglichen, die in der Livemusik unterrepräsentiert sind. …

opportunities.title: Artists retreat
opportunities.details: Boathouse invites all creatives – visual artists, painters, sculptors, illustrators, designers, photographers, filmmakers, screen and playwrights, novelists, musicians, performance artists, dancers and choreographers, curators and creative thinkers to join us at The Artist Retreat for a self-led residency. The residency is based in “Boathouse”, a critically acclaimed building surrounded by lush greenery and birds. The rooms are large, spacious and restful invoking calm. The house provides many nooks and corners for artists to work together or in isolation. Situated near the Nal Sarovar and Thol Bird sanctuary, the house rings of songs by many birds in winter. Surrounded by green wetlands the Boathouse is an ideal place for working, contemplating, reading or just feeling lost in nature. The historic city of Ahmedabad is a UNESCO world heritage site, besides this there are buildings by modern masters Le Corbusier, Louis Kahn and B V Doshi. The Residency is ideal for those who wish to work or contemplate in peace or those who wish to network with other artists and learn from the vast resources of internationally acclaimed design institutes in Ahmedabad. Duration of residency Artists can stay up to two weeks to two months. Accommodation The Boathouse is a modern house, built in 2017, on the principles of sustainable architecture. At the heart of the residency is a 70 m² acoustically treated studio, originally conceived as a professional recording studio. Today it serves as a flexible environment for artistic research and production, particularly suited for sound art, moving image, video art, performance, installation and emerging media. Rather than offering only accommodation and studio space, Canteiro provides artists with access to an environment where research, experimentation and interdisciplinary practices are central to everyday life. Located in São Paulo—one of the world’s largest and most dynamic cultural centers—the residency connects artists to an active ecosystem of exhibitions, independent spaces, curators, researchers and international collaborations. The conceptual framework of the residency begins with a simple question: How do we live together? The designated project sites encompass ten diverse locations that shape the character of Tokyo: a historic temple in the city center, a cutting-edge business district, a traditional neighborhood alley, a rare surviving small-scale wooden building, a bustling train station, and an entertainment venue. Cruce encourages independence, cultural diversity, and pluralism. It promotes new models of living and alternative ways of thinking by offering participants the conditions to develop their projects while experiencing the rhythm and traditions of southern Spain. Participants can access studios, coworking areas, and event spaces, all within Centro Negra — AADK Spain’s headquarters — where contemporary creation and community converge. Operating within an industrial open-studio warehouse containing 13 independent creative workspaces, our core objective is to provide international visual artists and researchers with the physical space, critical dialogue, and local network necessary to execute ambitious projects. The residency is strategically structured around a dual-location urban concept: residents live in the central, trend-setting historic district of Malasaña—ideal for cultural immersion—and work in Carabanchel, the recognized epicenter of Madrid’s underground contemporary art movement. opportunities.title: Desert 23s arts ecology research residency
opportunities.details: This residency and research programme in the Atacama Desert, Chile invites artists and researchers to develop their work within a landscape shaped by climate, geological time and living cultural knowledge. Through field visits, collaborative activities, shared sessions and time for individual practice, the programme creates an immersive context for inquiry. It offers space to learn with the territory, build relationships and think critically within complex and fragile desert ecologies. This environment offers perspectives on both local dynamics and broader planetary processes, opening questions about how creative practice can reconfigure our relations with the natural world. Our objectives are to support the development of artistic work and research that engage with specific territories while reflecting on wider planetary questions. To cultivate a shared space for living, exchange and collective reflection between artists, researchers and local contexts. To encourage site-responsive, environmentally attentive practices that honour and respect local knowledge, ecologies and cultural patrimony. LOCATION The residency takes place near San Pedro de Atacama, within the wider territory of the Atacama Desert in northern Chile, close to the ecosystems of the Reserva Nacional Los Flamencos. opportunities.details: Open Call At the meeting point of South and Central America, dense rainforests merge with coastal mangroves and the Caribbean Sea. This transitional region — shaped by complex ecologies, cultural histories, and ongoing global pressures — holds both immense biodiversity and a layered human presence. Amidst these vibrant landscapes, our residency offers space for reflective creative practice connected to the surrounding ecologies and contemporary challenges of the region. As participants spend time immersed in these living environments, they are invited to reflect on broader questions of coexistence, interdependence, and how global environmental shifts are entangled with local realities. Rather than proposing solutions, the residency offers time and space to listen, observe, and respond through artistic practice — situated within the living complexity of the territory. Residency Program Our site-responsive residencies offer a carefully balanced structure combining guided experiences and self-directed time. Participants are invited to engage with place through field visits, reflective practice, and scheduled sessions with long-term local collaborators who share perspectives and practices connected to the land. Each program offers time for artistic inquiry within distinct ecological and cultural contexts, supporting reflective processes that consider our relationships with land, ecologies, and one another. opportunities.title: Patagonia verde 43s arts ecology research residency creative practice in dialogue with land ecologies planetary change
opportunities.details: Open Call Patagonia, at the world’s edge, is a land where boundaries of reality extend into realms of wonder and possibility. Here time unfolds with patience, and colossal forces of nature collide. Home to ancient forests, expansive ecological corridors, winding river networks, and glacier fields, this terrain nurtures life in its most resilient forms. Stories embedded in this land, enriched by the lore and beliefs of inhabitants both past and present, teach us to value the earth as a mentor, and not merely a resource. Secluded ecosystems serve as natural laboratories and examples of regeneration and hope here can reshape our view of nature and redefine our role within it. Engaging with this territory also requires facing its complexities, including global issues of climate change, shrinking glaciers, dwindling water supplies, and unsustainable growth. More than a geographical location; Patagonia offers a compelling narrative of human and nature’s coexistence and challenges today. We encourage our residents to explore these concerns throughout their time with us. Engaging in meaningful relationships within the territory as they work on creative research projects that allow us to reflect on a future where balance could be restored. In Patagonia – where the earth´s voice resonates, we hope to find the courage to listen and answer its call. opportunities.title: Japan new year retreat
opportunities.details: The BONFIRE Retreats are born from a desire to share our gaze and our deep connection to specific territories around the world. Landscapes, cultures, and energies that have transformed our lives and our artistic practice, and that we now wish to experience with you. Each edition is curated with attention and unfolds in a carefully chosen location, inviting a small group of creators into a slow, generous, and respectful way of relating to both the human and the more-than-human. For the NEW YEAR EDITION we are beyond excited to invite you into one of the oldest living cultures on earth. A place where, for thousands of years, rituals and gestures have been cultivated until the sacred and the everyday became almost inseparable. A cosmology shaped by Zen Buddhism, Shinto, and ancient animism, felt in the preparation of a cup of tea, the silence of a garden, respect for a tree, the making of an object, the entrance to a shrine, or the simple act of bowing. What Japan gives us is a different way of paying attention. And with it, a different way of inhabiting the world. The time has come to slide open the doors and welcome you in. Let Japan guide you. Duration of residency 10 days / 9 nights Accommodation Set between mountains and crossed by the Kamo River, Kyoto is a city where time folds differently. opportunities.title: Fall residency
opportunities.details: The Ruby Mountain Project (RMP) Artist Residency is a multidisciplinary, land-based program in the extraordinary Mojave Desert focused on creativity, community, connection, and land stewardship. The residency supports artists in all stages with particular encouragement for BIPOC, LGBTQIA2S+. Residencies run from September through May and typically last three weeks, with shorter and longer stays available. Cohorts generally include up to three artists and provide private or outdoor studio space, basic accommodations, communal facilities, and access to select tools and equipment. The fee-based program uses a sliding-scale model, with limited work-trade opportunities available to reduce costs. Programming includes cohort dinners, community gatherings, nature activities, director check-ins, and optional public workshops or presentations. Each residency concludes with an open studio opportunity for artists to share their work with the local community. The program prioritizes an inclusive, supportive environment and encourages meaningful relationships between artistic practice, community, and the Mojave Desert landscape. Duration of residency 1-3 weeks Accommodation The well-curated vintage travel trailers have kitchens with sinks, gas stoves and counter space. Beds are double sized mattresses and include linens and blankets. Tents are welcome. Everyone has access to the outdoor shower, pit toilet and outdoor kitchen.
